info.name: Velmora app API v1.0.0
info.description: The Velmora shop API for the mobile apps. JSON only. Errors are RFC 9457 application/problem+json with a stable `code`. Money is {amount_minor, currency, formatted}. Send Accept-Language: bn or en, and X-App-Platform / X-App-Version so an app that is too old can be told to update. Made from docs/api/openapi.json by `php artisan api:collection`; do not edit by hand. Pick the "Velmora (local)" environment, run Auth > Log in, and the access token is saved for you. Placing an order needs a fresh Idempotency-Key per order (filled in); resend the same key only to retry the same order.

request.description: The default address first.
The division, district and upazila must belong together (`GET /geo/...`). The first address, or one sent with `make_default`, becomes the default.
The policies a new customer must accept, with the release number to send back as `policy_releases` when registering or when a phone code creates the account. Empty when nothing has been published.
Makes a customer account and emails a verification link. Never returns a token: the person signs in afterwards. The answer is the same whether or not the address already has an account.

item.name: Sign in with email or phone and password

request.description: Customers only. An unknown account, a wrong password, a locked or disabled account and a staff account all get the same `auth.invalid_credentials`. Too many tries get 429 with Retry-After.

exec: if (d && d.access_token) { pm.environment.set("access_token", d.access_token); pm.environment.set("refresh_token", d.refresh_token); }
// the refresh token works ONCE: always store the new one that comes back, and never send an old one again.

item.name: Ask for a sign-in code by text message

request.description: Always answers 202 for a valid number, whether or not it has an account. `cooling_down` means a code was sent a moment ago and is still valid.

item.name: Sign in with a text-message code

request.description: A new number makes a new customer account, exactly as on the website. A wrong, expired or used code, a locked number and a staff number all get the same `auth.otp_invalid`.

exec: if (d && d.access_token) { pm.environment.set("access_token", d.access_token); pm.environment.set("refresh_token", d.refresh_token); }
// the refresh token works ONCE: always store the new one that comes back, and never send an old one again.

item.name: Swap the refresh token for a new pair

request.description: Each refresh token works once. Using one a second time ends the whole sign-in (`auth.refresh_reused`), because it means a copy was stolen.

exec: if (d && d.access_token) { pm.environment.set("access_token", d.access_token); pm.environment.set("refresh_token", d.refresh_token); }
// the refresh token works ONCE: always store the new one that comes back, and never send an old one again.

item.name: Ask for a password reset link

request.description: Always answers 202, whether or not the address has an account.

item.name: Set a new password with the emailed token

request.description: Every signed-in device is signed out. A used, expired or wrong token is a validation error on `token`.

item.name: Send a code to confirm it is you

request.description: For people who have no password. The code goes to their verified phone.
Send the password, or the code from /auth/reauth/code. For the next few minutes this sign-in may do sensitive things (change the password, later: email, phone, delete the account).

`sku` is the `variant.sku` of a service. `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Dhaka days, today up to the service's booking horizon; default tomorrow) gives that day's really-free times, up to 60. A time is only a promise once you hold it.

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Holds that time for a few minutes and puts the booking in the cart; pay for the cart to confirm it. `resource` and `start` come from a slot (`resource`, `starts_at`). Somebody else was faster: `booking.slot_taken`. A guest gets a `cart_token` (also in the `X-Cart-Token` header) to send on cart and checkout calls. Holding another time for the same service replaces the earlier hold.
What is coming first (soonest first), then the past (newest first). Each says what I can do (`can_cancel`, `can_reschedule`, `can_complete`) and what cancelling would cost (`if_cancelled`).
Under the service's cancellation terms: `if_cancelled` on the booking says what it would cost and what is refunded.

item.name: Move a booking to another time

request.description: `start` is the `starts_at` of a free time for the same service and person (`GET /services/{sku}/slots?resource=`). Allowed only with enough notice and while moves are left.
After the time has come.

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Empty (and no token) for a guest without one. Lines carry `problem` (`unavailable`, `insufficient_stock`) and `price_changed_from` when a price moved since the item was added: show them, and call `/cart/acknowledge` once the person has seen the new price.

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: `variant` is the `variant.id` of a product. Adding an item already in the cart raises its quantity. Services are not added here: they are booked at a time.

exec: const t = pm.response.headers.get("X-Cart-Token"); if (t) { pm.environment.set("cart_token", t); }   // a guest's cart: send it back on every cart and checkout call

switch on when signed in

request.description: 0 takes the item out.

switch on when signed in
a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: A code that cannot be used is `coupon.invalid` with the reason in `detail` (unknown, expired, minimum spend, already used up).

switch on when signed in
a guest's cart; leave off when signed in

request.description: Marks the price changes in the cart as seen, so they stop being flagged.

item.name: Bring a guest cart into my account

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in

request.description: Send right after signing in, with the `X-Cart-Token` the app held as a guest. The items join the account's cart under the cart's own rules; the guest cart is then gone. Returns the account's cart.
Active categories only, as a tree in the shop's own order (three levels deep at most in practice). A category under a hidden one is hidden too.
With its trail from the top (`ancestors`) and its direct sub-categories.
Active brands, by name.
A hand-picked set of products (for example for a festival). The products themselves: `GET /products?filter[collection]=slug`.

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Send the contact and the address (a saved `address.id`, or the address typed in full) and, optionally, the delivery and payment you want to see priced. The answer is what would be charged, how it would be delivered, the ways to pay, whether a phone code is needed (large cash orders), and the policies to accept. Nothing is saved and nothing is reserved. For a cart with nothing to deliver (digital goods, services) send `contact.name` and `contact.phone` instead of an address.

item.name: Send a code to the phone

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: For a large cash-on-delivery order the phone number must be confirmed first. Sends a 6-digit code by text message. `status` is `sent` or `cooling_down` (a code was sent a moment ago and still works).

item.name: Confirm the phone with the code

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Every failure (wrong, expired, used up) answers the same `auth.otp_invalid`. On success you get a `phone_proof`: send it with the order. It is good for `expires_in` seconds and only for this phone number.

header.description: a guest's cart; leave off when signed in
a new key for each order; resend the SAME key only to retry the same order
switch on when signed in

request.description: Needs an `Idempotency-Key` header (8 to 100 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` or `-`; make a new one for each order the person confirms and reuse it for every retry of that same order). The same key can never make a second order, however many times it is sent. `expected_total` is the `grand_total.amount_minor` the person was shown; if the real total differs the order is NOT placed and the answer is 409 `checkout.totals_changed` with the fresh `quote`. `next` is `pay` when the chosen method is online and the order awaits payment, otherwise `none`. A guest also gets `order_token` (valid 30 days, for this one order): send it as `X-Order-Token` to pay for, view, track and get the invoice of that order. A signed-in customer gets `null` (their sign-in is the proof).

exec: const d = (pm.response.json() || {}).data; if (d && d.order_token) { pm.environment.set("order_token", d.order_token); }

request.description:
Everything an app needs before it shows anything: languages, currency, how prices are shown, the oldest app version still served,
how to reach the shop, and the pages (policies, help) it can link to. Cached for a few minutes; send If-None-Match to ask cheaply.
Does nothing (and still answers 202) if the address is already verified.

item.name: Ask to change the email address

request.description: A confirmation link goes to the NEW address. The change happens when that link is opened and the person is signed in as the account owner (the link opens the shop's website; sign in there if asked). The answer is the same whether or not the address belongs to someone else.

item.name: Send a code to a new phone number

request.description: The code goes to the NEW number. `status` is `sent` or `cooling_down` (a code was sent a moment ago and still works).
Send the same `phone` and the code. A wrong, expired or used code is `auth.otp_invalid`; a number that belongs to another account is a validation error on `phone`.

item.name: Register this phone for push messages

request.description: Send it after every sign-in and whenever the push token changes. Registering the same token again updates it (200); a new one is created (201). Signing out removes the device.

item.name: Stop push messages to this phone

request.description: `division` is an id from `/geo/divisions`; an unknown one is 404.
`district` is an id from `/geo/districts`; an unknown one is 404.

`state` is `available`, `limit_reached`, `expired`, `revoked` or `not_ready`. `left` is the downloads still allowed (`unlimited` when there is no limit). `keys_needed` / `keys_ready` count licence keys.

Uses one download and answers a short-lived address for the file (`url`, valid until `expires_at`, about a minute): fetch it straight away; the address is not kept. A purchase with no downloads left is `entitlement.limit_reached`, an expired one `entitlement.expired`, a revoked one `entitlement.revoked`, one with no file yet `entitlement.unavailable`; none of these uses a download.
The keys given to this purchase, never kept by a cache. Keys still being prepared are `entitlement.unavailable`.
Needs a recent confirmation (`auth.reauth_required` otherwise: call /auth/reauth first). Every other signed-in device is signed out; this one stays.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Items at the price they were bought at, the delivery address, how it was paid, and `available_actions` (`pay`, `track`, `invoice`, and for the owner `cancel`, `request_cancel`, `reorder`, `return`): show a button for exactly these. A guest sends `X-Order-Token` instead of signing in; the phone number is then masked.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: A short-lived signed link to the printable receipt (open it in a browser or share it). It stops working after `expires_at`; ask again for a new one.
Newest first, `limit` (1 to 50, default 20) at a time. `meta.next_cursor` is `null` on the last page; otherwise send it back as `cursor`. Only the signed-in customer's own orders.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in

request.description: If the order may still be cancelled by its owner (not yet confirmed, not paid, nothing sent) it is cancelled now (`result: cancelled`). If it is already being handled but nothing has shipped, a cancellation request goes to the shop (`result: requested`, 202). Otherwise `order.not_cancellable` with the reason in `detail`.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in

request.description: Puts the order's items in the cart at today's price, under the cart's own rules. Each line says whether it went in, and why not if it did not. Nothing is bought and no stock is held; fetch `GET /cart` next.

Published pages only. `body_html` is the shop's own sanitised HTML: show it in a web view or an HTML-capable text view. A page that exists only in another language, or only as a draft, is 404 (`page.not_found`). `GET /config` lists the pages and their slugs.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Needs an `Idempotency-Key` header. Answers `redirect_url`: open it in an in-app browser; the person pays at the gateway. When the browser closes, or comes back to the shop's site, call `GET /orders/{id}/payment` (and `POST /orders/{id}/payment/verify` to ask the gateway right away). A failed or abandoned attempt can be retried by calling this again with a new key. An order that is paid, cancelled or not an online order answers `order.already_paid`.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: What this server has recorded, never what the app says. `paid` is true only after the gateway confirmed the full amount in the right currency. `can_pay` says whether starting a payment makes sense now.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Makes the server ask the gateway about this order's open attempts (server to server) instead of waiting for the gateway's own notification. Safe to repeat: a payment is only ever applied once. Returns the same as the status call.
`history` is the last ten changes (what, when, from where).

Send both `email` and `sms` every time (true = yes, please). `push` (offers and news as push messages) is optional: leave it out and the answer is not changed. Messages about the customer's own orders are pushed to every signed-in phone whatever is chosen here; signing out of a phone stops them. `quiet_from` and `quiet_to` (`HH:MM`, Dhaka time) come together or not at all; marketing messages wait out these hours.
Newest first. `blockers` lists what stands in the way of erasing the account right now (for example an order still on its way).

item.name: Ask for a copy of my data

request.description: Built in the background; one a day. When `status` is `ready`, fetch it with the download call.
The copy itself, as a JSON file, sent only to this signed-in, freshly confirmed caller (never as a link anyone could open). Kept 7 days; every download is recorded.

item.name: Ask for my account to be erased

request.description: Send `understand: true`. The shop reviews it; it is refused while an order is still being handled or a booking is still to come. You can cancel while it waits.
Only while it is still waiting.

One scope at most: the whole shop, a category (with its sub-categories) or a collection. Narrow it with `filter[brand]`, `filter[type]`, `filter[in_stock]`, `filter[price_min]` / `filter[price_max]` (minor units, e.g. poisha) and `filter[attr][code]`. Sort by `newest`, `price_asc`, `price_desc` or `popular`. `meta.facets` tells which filters would leave something to show.

Everything the product page shows for one variant. Choose a variant by sending `options[code]=value` (for example `options[size]=m`); the answer says which values are selected, which would be in stock, the price of that variant and the `variant.id` to put in the cart. A slug from another language or an old spelling still finds the product; use the `slug` in the answer from then on.
Same category first, then same brand, then newest. Never the product itself.
`name` is required; `birth_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, in the past) is optional and cleared when empty.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in

request.description: `position` is the line's place in the order (first line is 1): send it back to name the line. `left` is how many may still be returned, `until` the last day, `open` whether it can be asked for now. `reasons` are the codes to choose from.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in

request.description: Only delivered items, inside the return window, and not more than were delivered. A refused request is `return.not_eligible` with the reason in `detail`.
Newest first, with their items and the shop's note once decided.
Only while the shop has not acted on it.
Of the product a variant belongs to: send the product's `variant.id` as `variant`. Published reviews only, newest first, 10 a page (`page`); `stats` counts them all.
With their state (`pending`, `published`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`) and, when the shop rejected or removed one, the reason.

item.name: What I can review in an order

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in

request.description: The lines of my own order I may review now (paid or delivered, not cancelled, soon enough), and whether I already have. Somebody else's order is 404.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in

request.description: 1 to 5 stars, an optional headline and 10 to 2,000 characters; no links; the same text twice in a month is refused; 5 an hour. It shows only after the shop approves it. Not a buyer, not yet delivered, too long ago: `review.not_eligible`; already reviewed: `review.duplicate`.

`q` is 1 to 100 characters. Results come best first (`sort=relevance`, the default) or in any other order, and take the same `filter[...]`, `page` and `per_page` as the product list. When the exact words find nothing but a close spelling does, `meta.corrected_query` says which one was used. The first page of a real search is logged (text, language and result count only) to improve the shop.
Product names as someone types: at least 2 characters, at most 10 suggestions. Never logged and not personal, so it may be cached for a minute.
`id` is the `id` from the list (also the `session_id` given at sign-in). Somebody else's, an ended one or an unknown one is 404.
Most recently active first.
`category` is one of the codes from the list call. `order` (an order `id` of mine) is optional. 5 or more characters of text.
`mine` is true for my own messages. Notes the shop keeps for itself are never shown.

header.description: a guest's proof for this one order; leave off when signed in
switch on when signed in

request.description: Each parcel's stage in plain words, what is in it, the courier's tracking link, a timeline in the shop's own statuses, and what has not been sent yet. No address, phone numbers or courier notes. The signed-in owner, or a guest with the order's `X-Order-Token`.
`state` is `in_stock`, `out_of_stock` or `unavailable`. `can_alert` says "tell me when it is back" makes sense; `alerts` lists the ones already waiting.
`variant` is a product's `variant.id`. Saving it again changes nothing. Up to 200 items; services cannot be saved.

item.name: Move an item to the cart

request.description: Puts it in the cart at the smallest quantity it allows, under the cart's own rules. If it cannot go in, the reason is in `detail`.

item.name: Tell me when it is back

request.description: For an item that is out of stock. You are told once, by push, text or email, and can ask again.
